definitions.explanation: a thin stick used by a conductor to direct an orchestra, choir, or other musical ensemble

examples.japanese: {指揮者|しきしゃ}が{指揮棒|しきぼう}を{振|ふ}った。
{指揮棒|しきぼう}の{動|うご}きに{合|あ}わせて{演奏|えんそう}する。
examples.english: Play in time with the movements of the baton.

examples.japanese: この{指揮棒|しきぼう}は{軽|かる}くてバランスが{良|よ}い。
examples.english: This baton is light and well-balanced.

notes:
USAGE:
The baton (タクト from German Taktstock is also used) is typically 10-15 inches long. Some conductors prefer not to use a baton and conduct with their hands only.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {指揮棒|しきぼう}を{振|ふ}る (to conduct; literally "wave the baton")
- {指揮棒|しきぼう}を{握|にぎ}る (to hold the baton; take up conducting)

RELATED TERMS:
- {指揮者|しきしゃ} (conductor)
- {指揮|しき} (conducting; direction)
- タクト (takt - baton, from German)
